_purpose: Executable test cases (EC) for UC2 (Live Stream Pause State) — runnable expansion of the scenarios. Per scenario: 1 success EC + exactly one alternative EC per expected.alternative[] entry.
_id_note: EC- = Executable Case. Chain: AC → SC → EC. (TC- = L3 condition; SC- = scenario.)

cases.name: [Live player] Verify pausing shows the ▶ overlay, keeps chat live, and tap-outside dismisses without seeking (paused at live edge)
preconditions: watching a live stream at the live edge (room.status = live)
(mobile) controls overlay revealed per UC1 / (desktop) direct-tap pause available
steps: Watch a live stream at the live edge (room.status = live) with the controls overlay revealed
Pause via the central pause button
Assert: the central ▶ button overlay is shown as the pause indicator (no separate badge/banner)
Assert: chat keeps receiving new messages in real time
Tap outside the play button
Assert: the overlay dismisses and the stream stays paused (position unchanged, no seek)
cases.expected_result: Pausing shows the central ▶ overlay as the pause indicator, chat keeps running live, and tapping outside the play button dismisses the overlay while the stream stays paused.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the pause overlay shows no ±10s seek controls (Live stream)
preconditions: watching a live stream at the live edge (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream (room.status = live) at the live edge
Assert: the pause overlay shows NO ±10s seek controls
cases.expected_result: The Live pause overlay shows NO ±10s seek controls (seeking is not applicable to a Live stream — BR-01).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify tapping ON the play button resumes playback (not the tap-outside dismiss)
preconditions: a paused live stream with the ▶ overlay visible (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream and reveal the ▶ overlay
Tap ON the play button
Assert: playback resumes (distinct from the tap-outside dismiss)
cases.expected_result: Tapping ON the play button resumes playback (distinct from the tap-outside dismiss).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the ▶ overlay is the only pause indicator (no separate badge/banner)
preconditions: a paused live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream at the live edge
Assert: no separate badge/banner is rendered — the ▶ overlay is the only pause-state indicator
cases.expected_result: There is no separate badge/banner — the ▶ overlay is the only pause-state indicator.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify resume seeks to ≈ the live edge within tolerance, dismisses the overlay, and keeps chat uninterrupted (paused live stream)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (chat kept running during the pause)
steps: Pause a live stream at the live edge (chat kept running during the pause, paused ~0:30 behind live)
Resume via the play button
Assert: playback seeks to ≈ the current live edge within tolerance (a few seconds behind live is OK) — NOT exact-live and NOT the paused offset
Assert: the ▶ overlay dismisses
Assert: chat is uninterrupted (no missed/replayed messages)
cases.expected_result: Resuming seeks to the current live edge (≈ live within normal buffering tolerance, never the paused position); the ▶ overlay dismisses and chat is uninterrupted.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify resume never returns to the previous paused offset (paused live stream)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (chat kept running during the pause)
steps: Pause a live stream so the paused offset is ~0:30 behind live
Resume via the play button
Assert: playback does NOT resume from the previous paused offset
cases.expected_result: Playback never resumes from the previous paused offset.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the resume target is near-live within tolerance, not exact-live (CONF-07)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (chat kept running during the pause)
steps: Pause then resume a live stream
Assert: the resume target is near live within tolerance — a few seconds behind live is expected, NOT exact-live (CONF-07)
cases.expected_result: The resume target is asserted as 'near live within tolerance' — a few seconds behind live is expected, not exact-live (CONF-07).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a room ending during a pause leaves paused for the ended state with no frozen frame (terminal wins)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream (room.status = live)
Mock: flip SDK room.status live → ended during the pause
Assert: the player leaves the paused state and shows the ended state (terminal wins)
Assert: the viewer is not left on a frozen frame (explicit ended feedback)
cases.expected_result: When the room transitions to ended/recorded during a pause, the player leaves paused and shows the terminal state — the terminal state always wins over paused, and the viewer is never left on a frozen frame.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a not-yet-ready recording shows 'Livestream ended' with no processing state (recording not ready)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream
steps: Pause a live stream, then flip room.status to ended with the recording not yet ready
Assert: 'Livestream ended' is shown, with NO intermediate 'processing' state
cases.expected_result: Recording not yet ready → 'Livestream ended' is shown, with NO intermediate 'processing' state.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a room that becomes recorded shows the recorded/VOD state (room recorded)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream
steps: Pause a live stream, then flip room.status to recorded
Assert: the player shows the recorded/VOD state
cases.expected_result: Room becomes recorded → the player shows the recorded/VOD state.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a simultaneous pause + host-end race resolves to ended (terminal wins, staged manually)
preconditions: watching a live stream (room.status = live)

test_data.race: pause + host-end at the same instant

steps: Stage a simultaneous pause + host-end (host ends the room at the same instant the user pauses)
Assert: the race resolves to the ended state (terminal wins over paused)
cases.expected_result: A simultaneous pause + host-end race resolves to ended (terminal wins) — staged manually (TC-UC2-07c).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the default live-edge state shows no pause indicator with LIVE badge, viewer count, and live chat intact (before any pause)
preconditions: a live stream (room.status = live) is playing at the live edge
the viewer has not yet paused
steps: Render the live player at the live edge (room.status = live) without pausing
Assert: no ▶ pause indicator is present
Assert: the LIVE badge + viewer count render as-is; chat is live
cases.expected_result: Before any pause, no pause indicator is shown; the LIVE badge and viewer count render as-is (unaffected by this feature) and chat is live.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify mobile web offers no pause control on a Live stream (web-mobile)
preconditions: a viewer on mobile web watching a Live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Render the Live player in a mobile-web viewport (room.status = live)
Assert: no pause control is offered (no pause affordance in the player chrome)
cases.expected_result: On mobile web, a live stream offers no pause control — pause/resume of an active Live stream is not available on web-mobile (standing platform boundary, not a bug).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify web-desktop presents the pause control (web-desktop, 1-step pause)
preconditions: a viewer on web-desktop watching a Live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Render the Live player in a web-desktop viewport
Assert: the pause control IS present (single-tap 1-step pause)
cases.expected_result: On web-desktop the pause control IS present (1-step pause).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify iOS / Android present the pause control (2-step reveal-then-pause)
preconditions: a viewer on iOS / Android (UIKit) watching a Live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Open the Live player on iOS / Android (UIKit)
Tap once to reveal controls, then tap the central button to pause
Assert: the pause control IS present (2-step reveal-then-pause)
cases.expected_result: On iOS / Android the pause control IS present (2-step reveal-then-pause).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a multi-minute pause still resumes to ≈ the live moment within tolerance (long pause)
preconditions: the user paused a live stream for an extended period (minutes)
steps: Pause for several minutes on a real broadcast (room.status = live)
Resume via the play button
Assert: playback snaps to ≈ the current live moment within tolerance (NOT the paused position, NOT exact-live); a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable
cases.expected_result: After a long pause, resuming snaps to the current live moment regardless of the jump size — a brief buffering/loading state is acceptable while it catches up.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify jump size does not change the resume-to-live guarantee (long pause, large jump)
preconditions: the user paused a live stream for an extended period (minutes)
steps: Pause for a long period so the jump back to live is large, then resume
Assert: the size of the jump does not change the guarantee — playback never resumes from the paused position
cases.expected_result: The size of the jump does not change the guarantee — it never resumes from the paused position.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a long-pause resume lands ≈ live within tolerance (further behind still within guarantee)
preconditions: the user paused a live stream for an extended period (minutes)
steps: Pause for several minutes, then resume
Assert: resume lands ≈ live within tolerance — being further behind live after a long pause is still within the guarantee (NOT exact-live)
cases.expected_result: Resume lands ≈ live within tolerance (further behind after a long pause is still within the guarantee).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify chat and video re-align at the live moment on resume with no replay and no skip (resume after pause)
preconditions: the user paused for a while (chat kept running live throughout)
steps: Pause for a while with chat running live throughout
Capture chat message ids before resume (e.g. last id = msg_140)
Resume via the play button
Capture chat message ids after resume
Assert: no message is replayed (duplicate) and none is skipped (gap); chat is aligned at the live moment
cases.expected_result: On resume, chat and video are aligned at the live moment — no chat messages are replayed and none are skipped.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify before-vs-after message ids show no duplicate and no gap on resume (message id diff)
preconditions: the user paused for a while (chat kept running live throughout)

test_data.expected_diff: no duplicate id, no missing id

steps: Capture chat message ids before resume and after resume
Compare the before vs after id sets
Assert: no duplicate id (replay) and no missing id (gap)
cases.expected_result: Comparing message ids before vs after resume shows no duplicate (replay) and no gap (skip).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify after a long paused window chat is already at the live moment on resume (long pause, continuous chat)
preconditions: the user paused for a long window (chat kept running live continuously)
steps: Pause for a long window while chat keeps running continuously
Resume via the play button
Assert: on resume chat is already at the live moment and aligns with the video (no backlog replay)
cases.expected_result: After a long paused window with continuous chat, on resume chat is already at the live moment and aligns with the video.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify a network drop while paused shows Reconnecting, stays paused through recover, and resumes to ≈ live (network drop/recover)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream (room.status = live)
Mock: drop the network connection while paused
Assert: a 'Reconnecting' indicator (auto-retry, no manual button) is shown — not a no-feedback frozen frame
Mock: recover the network
Assert: the stream stays paused (no auto-resume)
Resume via the play button
Assert: playback snaps to ≈ the current live edge within tolerance (NOT exact-live, NOT the paused offset)
cases.expected_result: A network drop while paused shows a 'Reconnecting' indicator (auto-retry, no manual button); the stream stays paused through drop→recover (no auto-resume); on user resume it snaps to the current live edge.

cases.name: [Live player] Verify the stream never auto-resumes on network recover (stays paused until explicit resume)
preconditions: the user has paused a live stream (room.status = live)
steps: Pause a live stream, drop the network, then recover the network
Assert: the stream stays paused — it never auto-resumes on recover (no implicit toggle) until the user explicitly resumes
cases.expected_result: The stream never auto-resumes on network recover — it stays paused until the user explicitly resumes (no implicit toggle).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify iOS shows the Reconnecting scrim even while paused (iOS NWPathMonitor)
preconditions: a viewer on iOS has paused a live stream (room.status = live)
steps: On iOS, pause a live stream, then drop the device network (NWPathMonitor)
Assert: the 'Reconnecting' scrim shows even while paused
cases.expected_result: (iOS) the 'Reconnecting' scrim shows even while paused (device network via NWPathMonitor).

cases.name: [Live player] Verify web shows no overlay on a plain paused-video drop, only on broadcaster waitingReconnect (web)
preconditions: a viewer on web has paused a live stream (room.status = live)
steps: On web, pause a live stream and drop the local paused-video network
Assert: a plain paused-video drop shows no overlay
Mock: set SDK room.status = 'waitingReconnect' (broadcaster drop)
Assert: only the broadcaster-drop 'waitingReconnect' surfaces the reconnecting overlay
cases.expected_result: (web) a plain paused-video drop shows no overlay; only SDK room.status = 'waitingReconnect' (broadcaster drop) surfaces it.
